interpretation: Projected attack paths: not confirmed attacks, and not a likelihood assessment. An LLM placed techniques that MITRE ATT&CK documents this actor using onto the organization's own flow map, reasoning the way an adversary would. Technique ids, technique names and controls are sourced; the route, the step rationales and the access states are the model's projection. Each step's access is checked only for continuity — that an earlier step produced what the step needs — never for truth. A step that states no access falls back to a typical value for its tactic.

attack_sequence.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application on Customer console
attack_sequence.description: The Node.js web console is exposed to the internet and can be targeted with remote code execution exploits, bypassing the WAF.
success_indicators: Execution context within the web console container.
attack_sequence.precondition: The web console runs a vulnerable version of a framework or library.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: Internet-facing web application with an exploitable vulnerability.
assumptions: A zero-day or unpatched N-day vulnerability exists in the web console.
attack_sequence.control_note: Fox Kitten utilizes exploits that evade standard WAF signatures.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Fox Kitten has exploited known vulnerabilities in Fortinet, PulseSecure, and Palo Alto VPN appliances.

attack_sequence.name: Web Shell on Customer console
attack_sequence.description: A web shell is dropped into the React/Node.js web directory to maintain reliable remote access to the compromised container.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has code execution and write permissions in a web-accessible directory.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: Writable filesystem within the web application's root or static directories.
assumptions: The container filesystem is not completely read-only.
attack_sequence.control_note: The web shell traffic blends in with legitimate HTTPS telemetry and console traffic.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Fox Kitten has installed web shells on compromised hosts to maintain access.

attack_sequence.name: Credentials In Files on Customer console
attack_sequence.description: The attacker searches local configuration files and environment variables for the database credentials used by the web console.
attack_sequence.precondition: The web console holds credentials to authenticate to the telemetry database.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: Credentials stored in plaintext within container files or environment variables.
assumptions: Database credentials are not securely vaulted in memory and are accessible via files/env.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Fox Kitten has accessed files to gain valid credentials.

attack_sequence.name: Valid Accounts on Telemetry warehouse
attack_sequence.description: Using the stolen Postgres credentials, the attacker authenticates directly to the telemetry database over the declared internal flow.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker possesses valid service credentials for the database.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: Database accepts authentication using statically configured service accounts.
assumptions: The database firewall permits traffic originating from the web console IP.
attack_sequence.control_note: Bypasses the database firewall because the web console is an allowed source.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Fox Kitten has used valid credentials with various services during lateral movement.

attack_sequence.name: Data from Local System on Telemetry warehouse
attack_sequence.description: The attacker queries the TimescaleDB tables directly to extract regulated customer telemetry data.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has authenticated access to query the database tables.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: Database contains regulated customer telemetry data.
assumptions: The stolen service account has sufficient privileges to read the targeted tables.
attack_sequence.control_note: Column-level encryption is partial and can be bypassed or decrypted with the service account keys.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Fox Kitten has searched local system resources to access sensitive documents.

attack_sequence.name: Valid Accounts on Source control and pipeline definitions
attack_sequence.description: The attacker uses compromised developer credentials and hijacked session tokens to log into the source control management system.
success_indicators: Authenticated access to repository code and pipeline definitions.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has acquired valid credentials and an active session token to bypass MFA.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: Internet-facing SCM relies on user authentication and session cookies.
assumptions: Attacker has successfully phished or purchased valid SCM session tokens.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Fox Kitten has used valid credentials with various services during lateral movement.

attack_sequence.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter on Self-hosted build runner
attack_sequence.description: By modifying a GitHub Actions workflow in the SCM, the attacker forces the self-hosted CI runner to execute arbitrary shell scripts.
success_indicators: Arbitrary code execution on the CI runner.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has permissions to commit code or modify pipeline definitions in the SCM.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: CI runner automatically executes scripts defined in the SCM pipeline.
assumptions: Branch protection and required reviews can be bypassed using an unprotected branch or compromised admin account.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Fox Kitten has used a Perl reverse shell to communicate with C2.
attack_sequence.state_check: gap — needs network_reach on ci_runner; the declared flow to it comes from scm, which no earlier step takes control of, so the path depends on scm acting for the attacker. Path holds user_credential, network_reach on scm

attack_sequence.name: Network Service Discovery on Self-hosted build runner
attack_sequence.description: From the CI runner, the attacker scans the internal network to identify the IP address and port of the Vault service.
success_indicators: Knowledge of the Vault service network location.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has code execution on the CI runner.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The CI runner resides in a zone with network line-of-sight to internal services.
assumptions: Network scanning tools are available or can be downloaded onto the CI runner.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Fox Kitten has used tools including NMAP to conduct broad scanning to identify open ports.

attack_sequence.name: Exploitation of Remote Services on Secrets manager
attack_sequence.description: The attacker exploits the overly permissive, unauthenticated HTTP flow from the CI runner to Vault to extract secrets.
success_indicators: Access to highly sensitive secrets and tokens stored in Vault.
attack_sequence.precondition: An unauthenticated flow exists between the CI runner and Vault.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: Vault accepts unauthenticated requests from the CI runner's IP address.
assumptions: The unauthenticated flow allows reading secrets, not just initiating authentication.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: Fox Kitten has exploited known vulnerabilities in remote services including RDP.
